- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. <function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. - pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. - figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

Search this repository (a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann fashion brand) for anything related to three related PDP features: (1) "size selector" / size selection UI, (2) "find my size" / fit finder / size guide, and (3) size "recommendation" / recommended size / fit recommendation.

content.text:
I have everything needed for a thorough report.

## Summary of findings

The three PDP size features are **all handled by one third-party vendor: Measmerize** (`measmerize.com`). It is not True Fit, Fit Analytics, or Bold Metrics — none of those three vendors are referenced anywhere in the repo (source or docs). Per the docs, Measmerize powers both "Find My Size" (recommendation → "Recommended: Size X" CTA) and the size-guide overlay, with a Contentful-managed size guide as fallback.

**Critically: there is NO React/UI implementation of any of these features in `overrides/`.** No product-detail page, no size-selector, swatch-group, variation-attributes, find-my-size, size-guide, or fit component has been created or overridden. The only *code* landed so far is infra plumbing (CSP allowlist + an env var); everything else is design documentation. The actual size-selector UI still lives entirely in the untouched upstream base template.

### Real code (implemented / landed)

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`** — Real implementation. Adds Measmerize domains to the CSP so the widget can load. Comments: `// Measmerize sizing widget (PDP)` and `// Measmerize brand-specific CSS bundle`.
  - `script-src`: `client.measmerize.com`, `static.client.measmerize.com` (lines 31-33)
  - `style-src`: `static.client.measmerize.com` (lines 40-41)
  - `connect-src`: `client.measmerize.com`, `api.client.measmerize.com` (lines 71-73) — the last one is the SSR data-availability pre-check API.

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.env.sample`** (lines 203-208), **`.env`** (lines 62-63), **`.env.shared`** (lines 32-33) — Real config. Defines `MEASMERIZE_BRAND_CODE=b38fac52-7328-45c9-9fd8-038fac4be58e` (the staging brand UUID, shared across Dev/SIT/UAT/Stage). Header comment: `# ── Measmerize (Find My Size widget on PDP) ──`. Note: this env var is **defined but not yet consumed** — a grep across `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr/`, and all JS config found zero code that reads `MEASMERIZE_BRAND_CODE`. So it is wired for the environment but no injection logic exists yet.

### Documentation (specs only — no code behind them yet)

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md`** — The integration design doc. Detailed spec of the SPA/React injection pattern (inject once in `useEffect` with empty deps, update `window.measmerize.script.productCode` on SPA nav, listen for `measmerize.widget.recommend` / `measmerize.widget.unavailable`, Contentful fallback, checkout.js on order-confirmation). Confirms "Modal Integration is the required path" (2026-07-06) — PWA owns the shell, injects via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. Contains staging + production brand codes. Section 7 flags a **blocking open item: consent approach (free-load + SDK opt-out vs. Didomi-gated script load)**.

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/vendor/measmerize.md`** — Vendor API reference (script URLs, script-tag attributes, DOM containers `#measmerize-button`/`#measmerize-modal`/`#measmerize-recommendation`, full custom-events table, `window.measmerize` global object, cookie categories, SSR pre-check endpoint).

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/pdp.md`** — PRD. §10 "Find My Size / Measmerize" (PRD-050-053) and §11 "Size Guide" (PRD-053-057). Key requirements: recommendation updates CTA to "Recommended: Size X" (PRD-050); size guide is a Measmerize slide-out overlay with Contentful fallback; cm/inches toggle (PRD-056); structured Contentful size-guide content type per product type (PRD-055). §7 lists supporting links **Find My Size** and **Size Guide** (PRD-021). Note: the generic size *selector* (per-size availability, OOS greying, "LOW" indicator) is described in §4/§6 and is served by the upstream base component, not a custom build.

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/temp/openItems.md`** — §17 (lines 145-147) restates the blocking consent open item; line 12 and line 37 track Measmerize among external systems needing per-env IDs.

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/architecture.md`** (line 247) and **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md`** (lines 56, 96, 289, 368, 440) — Architecture tables listing Measmerize as browser-direct PDP script injection, deferred behind LCP, "Consent approach unconfirmed — open item."

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/index.md`** (line 52) and **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/index.md`** (line 34) — index/reference entries pointing to the above.

### Upstream base-template files (copied dependency, NOT overridden — the current size selector)

These live in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` and provide the existing (generic Commerce Cloud) size/variant selector. None are copied into `overrides/`, so they are stock upstream:

- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx` — Hosts the size/variant selector; renders `SwatchGroup`/`Swatch` from `variationAttributes` (imports at lines 54-55; render loop ~line 682).
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/` (`index.jsx`, `swatch.jsx`, `index.test.js`) — the size/colour swatch UI primitives.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes.js`, `use-variation-params.js`, `use-controlled-variations.js` — variant/size selection state hooks.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/` (`index.jsx`, `partials/information-accordion.jsx`, etc.) — the base PDP; contains a "Size & Fit"-style information accordion but **no** Measmerize / Find My Size / size-recommendation logic.

### Stories / tests

No Storybook stories or tests for any size feature exist in `overrides/`. The only override stories are `overrides/app/components/button/index.stories.tsx` and `overrides/app/components/icons/icons.stories.tsx` (matched only on `fontSize` — false positives). `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx` also matched only on `fontSize`/`objectFit` — unrelated to sizing.

### Other vendors
Grep for `True Fit`, `Fit Analytics`, `Bold Metrics`, `fitFinder`/`fit finder` returned **zero hits** anywhere in the repo. Measmerize is the sole size-rec vendor.

### Bottom line
- Size *selector* UI: exists only as the untouched upstream base (`product-view` + `swatch-group`).
- Find My Size + Size Guide + size recommendation: **fully specced in docs, only partially plumbed in code** (CSP domains allowlisted + `MEASMERIZE_BRAND_CODE` env var defined). The env var is not yet read, and no script-injection hook, DOM containers, event listeners, CTA-update logic, or Contentful fallback component have been built. A blocking open item (consent approach) remains before implementation.

content.text:
I now have a complete cross-source picture. Here's the current state.

## TL;DR

All three features are **specced and decided but not yet built in code**. The size selector still runs on the untouched upstream base template; "Find My Size" + size recommendation + size guide are all delivered by a single confirmed vendor — **Measmerize** — for which only infra plumbing (CSP allowlist + one env var) has landed. Your own story, SFCC-92 (Size Selector), is currently **Blocked**.

---

## The vendor decision (settled)

**Measmerize** (`measmerize.com`) is the confirmed provider for *all three* of size recommendation, Find My Size, and the size guide. It is **not** True Fit / Fit Analytics / Bold Metrics — none of those appear anywhere. Decided points:

- **Modal/injection integration is the required path** (per [.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md](.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md), 2026-07-06) — the PWA owns the shell and injects the script on PDP; Measmerize owns the widget's look/feel and recommendation logic (out of SFCC scope).
- **Size guide hierarchy:** Measmerize overlay is primary (PRD-053); Contentful size-guide content is fallback **only where Measmerize has no data** for the product ([Contentful TSD, SFCC-249](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/346783750)).
- Integration ID collision resolved: Measmerize moved INT-033 → **INT-034** (2026-07-07).

## How the three features map to Jira

| Feature | Story | Status | Owner / Squad |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Size selector** + Add to Bag | [SFCC-92](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-92) | 🟡 **Blocked** | **You (Marcel)** / A |
| **Find My Size** CTA + Measmerize widget | [SFCC-101](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-101) | In Refinement | Jasmijn Tsang / A |
| **Size guide** slide-out (Size & Fit) | [SFCC-102](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102) | In Refinement | Jasmijn Tsang / A |
| Size-**recommendation** UX decisions | [SFCC-255](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-255) (subtask of 101) | To Do | Emma Kirwan |
| Related states (Coming/Back in Soon, Unavailable) | [SFCC-150](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-150) | In Refinement | Jasmijn Tsang / A |

All sit under the PDP epic [SFCC-5](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-5).

**Behaviour agreed** (SFCC-101 + design review notes in SFCC-255):
- PDP *always* shows a "Find Your Size" CTA. If Measmerize is configured for the product → CTA opens the Measmerize widget; if not → opens the SFCC/Contentful size-guide slide-out.
- Once Measmerize returns a recommendation, "Continue" selects that size on the PDP.
- Wording is **"Recommended / Recommendation"**; "Find your size" moves *down inside* the size selector once a recommendation is shown; changing the size clears "Recommended" and returns "Find your size" to its original position next to the selector.

## Code state (what's actually landed)

- ✅ **CSP allowlist** for Measmerize domains — [overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts](overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts) (`client.measmerize.com`, `static.client.measmerize.com`, `api.client.measmerize.com`).
- ✅ **`MEASMERIZE_BRAND_CODE`** env var defined in [.env.sample](.env.sample) / `.env.shared` (staging UUID) — **but not yet read by any code**.
- ❌ **No UI whatsoever** in `overrides/`: no `product-view`, `swatch-group`, `product-detail`, `find-my-size`, or `size-guide` override. The size selector today is entirely stock `@salesforce/retail-react-app` base template. No script-injection hook, event listeners, CTA-update logic, or Contentful fallback component exist yet.

## Open items / blockers ⚠️

1. **Consent gating is the key blocker.** How Measmerize is loaded under Didomi is still unconfirmed (free-load + SDK opt-out vs. Didomi-gated load). Flagged in [.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md §7](.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md) and as an open action on [Consent Management — Business Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/299433985): *"Confirm Measmerize Didomi purpose/category so the PWA can gate it correctly"* — owner Tell No Lies / Zimmermann.
2. **SFCC-92 (your story) is blocked** by the **Figma-to-React implementation spike** [SFCC-240](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-240) (Ready for Development, not done) and by Notify Me [SFCC-149](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-149). The earlier setup spike SFCC-205 is Done.
3. **101/102 still In Refinement** — not Ready for Development yet.
4. **SEO/LLM concern** noted in the functional-requirements sheet: a client-side Measmerize widget puts size-guide content outside the SSR HTML — unresolved.

## Two notes worth raising

- **"Recommendation" is ambiguous** in your question. Above is the **size** recommendation (Measmerize). If you also meant **product** recommendations ("You May Also Like" / "Complete the Look"), those are a *separate* Squad B track under Einstein — epic [SFCC-7](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-7), stories [SFCC-112](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-112)/[118](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-118)/[119](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-119), all still In Refinement/To Do. Let me know if you want that thread expanded.
- **Security flag:** the [SFCC-101](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-101) description contains **plaintext Measmerize docs-portal credentials** (username + password) and both staging *and production* brand IDs in the ticket body. That's worth scrubbing from Jira into a secrets store — happy to help draft that ask if useful.

Want me to go deeper on any one thread — e.g. what SFCC-92 needs to get unblocked, or the exact Measmerize injection pattern the integration doc prescribes?
